stem_book: An ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion from state I to state II followed by a reversible adiabatic expansion from state II to state III. The correct plot(s) representing the changes from state I to state III is(are) (P: pressure, V: volume, T: temperature, H: enthalpy, S: entropy) [options are the four plots shown]: (a) P vs V: hyperbola I→II, then a steeper falling curve II→III (b) P vs T: vertical drop I→II at constant T, then a curve II→III with P and T both decreasing (c) H vs S: horizontal I→II, then vertical rise II→III (H increasing at constant S) (d) T vs S: horizontal I→II, then vertical drop II→III (T decreasing at constant S)
reason: Options are graphs (figure needed). Official JEE Adv 2021 answer ABD.
work: Isothermal: T, H const, S↑, P↓ ⇒ (b),(d) first legs right; adiabatic: S const, T↓ so H↓ ⇒ (c) shows H rising ✗; P–V adiabat steeper ✓ ⇒ a, b, d
